opportunity_map.area: Inbound phone, one line, published 6:00am to 7:00/8:00pm seven days
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: The site publishes one business number, 907-235-7620, with no second line, no department routing and no answering service (verified structural absence, contact-1). One of the two named owners is 'Owner & Captain of The Irish', so during the fishing day a captain-owner is structurally not at a desk. AI could triage calls that arrive while both owners are unavailable, capture the caller and the reason, and route the money-governed ones to a human immediately. Honest caveat, this is also the channel FareHarbor Agent is described as covering, and it is the channel where weather and cancellation bad news lands, which the MDPI study warns against automating.

opportunity_map.area: Shared inbox, northcountrycharters@gmail.com, one Gmail for the whole operation
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: One inbox covers everything, with no routing published. AI could read what already arrives, classify it against the company's own published policy, and separate the messages that cost money from the ones that can wait. This needs no new channel and no new place for anyone to look.

opportunity_map.area: Cancellations and changes, the money-governed clock
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: Their FAQ sets hard thresholds, 50 percent deposit at 14 days or less, 100 percent of the charter rate at 24 hours or less or a no-show. The same FAQ says 'We don't always see voicemails or emails right away and every minute counts.' AI could stamp every inbound cancellation or change against those two lines the moment it arrives and make a human's phone ring, so lateness stops being a channel accident.

opportunity_map.area: Weather go or no-go and the notification fan-out
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: Weather cancellation before departure is a 100 percent refund, and leaving the dock without fishing is $30 per person, so weather is an operator-borne cost written into their own policy. AI could pre-draft the notification per party, assemble rebooking options, and track refund status against the two published rules. It should not deliver the news autonomously, the 467-participant MDPI study found booking intention fell further with an AI agent than a human in a negative-outcome scenario, 0.83 versus 0.54 points, and the authors recommend small operators keep a human escalation path.

opportunity_map.area: Freed-seat recovery on a perishable inventory
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: A charter seat is perishable and 'every minute counts' is their own wording. AI could match a seat freed by a cancellation to an interest list and push a first-come booking link. Flagged honestly, the resale motive is our structural inference, their quote proves urgency and not the resale intent, and no interest list is evidenced to exist.

The home page says 'Winter Hours Are Inconsistent, Leave a Voicemail', so the off-season channel is voicemail. Emerald Air Service runs FareHarbor for the current season plus a separate portal for 2027 advance bookings. AI could hold a 24/7 off-season answer and interest list grounded in their own published FAQ, and convert it when next-season dates open.

opportunity_map.area: Channel coverage versus the competitive set
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: Emerald Air Service publishes phone, text, WhatsApp, email and a contact form. North Country publishes phone, one shared inbox and voicemail. AI could make an SMS path actually staffable by two people rather than adding a channel nobody can watch. Note the verified market fact, no Homer or Kachemak Bay operator checked runs live chat, a chatbot or an AI phone line, so there is no local proof either way.

opportunity_map.area: Product mix, four products including a Guest Room
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: The home page lists exactly four things, Halibut Fishing, Combo Fishing, Salmon Fishing and a Guest Room. A charter guest is structurally a lodging prospect. AI could attach the room to a charter booking conversation. Evidence is thin, there is nothing verified about attach rate or that this is a problem today.

They maintain a detailed FAQ that carries policy, weather and cancellation rules, which is what a shop writes when it answers the same things repeatedly. RAG over their own published pages could deflect the routine ones. This is the single area with the highest overlap against FareHarbor Agent, which is described as answering guest questions across phone, email, chat, SMS, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp and checking live availability, on a platform they already pay for. We should not sell them this.

This is a do-not-automate zone, and saying so is part of the work. The business is independently listed on Yelp, TripAdvisor and Fish Alaska Magazine. The verified evidence here is a failure mode, a Which? and Guardian investigation found TripAdvisor's AI review summaries downplayed serious guest complaints. A 47-year-old family name in a small town is exactly the asset an AI-written reply can damage.

opportunity_map.area: Back office concentrated in one person
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: Their own page says 'Kathy is the co-owner and office manager, which loosely translates to: the person who handles everything no one else wants to deal with.' AI could take the recurring, mechanical parts of that load. The job is real and first-party, the specific tasks inside it are not published, so any build here has to start by observing rather than assuming.

Nothing, and this is a deliberate map entry. They already run FareHarbor with a BOOK NOW button, the same platform Smokey Bay Air, Emerald Air Service, Destination Alaska Charters and Bear Viewing Alaska run. They are at parity, not behind. Any proposal that tells them to fix their booking system is wrong on the facts.

FareHarbor Agent is real and shipping, and FareHarbor's own page says it 'is currently rolling out to a select group of operators'. FareHarbor publishes no independent measurement, no named operator and no before/after numbers for it. The honest AI-adjacent job here is to help them ask for the pilot and measure it, not to duplicate it.

Listed for completeness and explicitly unevidenced. No headcount is published on the site, the ZoomInfo figure was rejected as unverifiable, and no licensing or reporting obligation was verified in this package. Nothing may be proposed here without new research.

outcome: Turn more of the demand that already reaches one phone line and one shared inbox into paid seats, without adding a person. Measured three ways against a baseline that has to be created in the first week, because nothing in evidence logs any of it today. One, median minutes from a cancellation or change message landing on any channel to a human confirming it by phone, which is the standard their own FAQ sets. Two, booked seats per 100 inbound contacts. Three, seats freed inside the 14-day window that get resold before departure. Explicitly not the outcome, a chatbot being live, a phone being answered by a machine, or a dashboard existing. If those three numbers do not move, the build failed and we say so.

opportunities.job: When a guest sends a cancellation or a change, I need to see it inside the window that decides the money, because the charge changes at 14 days and again at 24 hours
opportunities.pain_source: FAQ verbatim, 'IF YOU NEED TO CANCEL please call us and confirm over the phone with us that you are cancelling. We don't always see voicemails or emails right away and every minute counts.' Plus FAQ, 'Short notice cancellations (14 days or less) are subject to a 50% deposit' and 'In the unlikely event of a last-minute cancellation of 24 hours or less OR a no-show... you will be charged 100% of the charter rate.' northcountrycharters.com/faq
opportunities.current_workaround: A written policy that asks the customer to route around the channel. They instruct guests to phone and confirm verbally rather than rely on the voicemail and email they already have.
opportunities.notes: The strongest evidence in the package and it is first-party, in writing, on their own site. It is evidence about a MESSAGE CHANNEL, not a statement that this business is overwhelmed, and no such statement exists anywhere. Satisfaction is not zero, the workaround genuinely works for any guest who reads the FAQ and calls. Importance and satisfaction are our estimates from cited structural evidence, not from customer interviews.

opportunities.job: When my season closes and my hours go inconsistent, I need next season's demand captured and converted rather than sitting in voicemail
opportunities.pain_source: Home page verbatim, 'Winter Hours Are Inconsistent, Leave a Voicemail'. Competitor verified, Emerald Air Service runs FareHarbor for the current season plus a separate portal for 2027 advance bookings, emeraldairservice.com
opportunities.current_workaround: Voicemail. The site tells off-season inquirers to leave one.
opportunities.notes: Timing is the interesting part. The season closes mid-September, so this window opens in roughly six weeks rather than closing. Caveat held honestly, Emerald's 2027 portal proves a competitor's choice, it does not prove this company's need.

opportunities.job: When weather kills or shortens a trip, I need every party told fast and offered a rebook, because I am the one eating the refund
opportunities.pain_source: FAQ verbatim, 'If a charter is cancelled before departure due to weather, there is a 100% refund' and 'If we leave the dock but find we were unable to fish due to weather, there is a nominal fee of $30/person which helps cover crew and fuel expenses.' northcountrycharters.com/faq
opportunities.current_workaround: The phone and the shared inbox. The site publishes no other notification path, no SMS, no answering service.
opportunities.notes: High importance, deliberately constrained solution space. The MDPI study of 467 participants is the direct counter-evidence, booking intention dropped 0.83 points with an AI agent versus 0.54 with a human in a negative-outcome scenario, and the authors recommend small tourism operators keep a human escalation path. Weather cancellation is precisely that moment, governed by real money in their published policy.

opportunities.job: When a seat frees up late, I need it filled before the boat leaves
opportunities.pain_source: FAQ verbatim, 'every minute counts', read against the 14-day and 24-hour charge thresholds. Market context, Central Charters and Tours runs a live 'There are 5 people looking at this charter' counter on FishingBooker, fishingbooker.com/charters/view/41714
opportunities.notes: Confidence discount applied. Their quote proves urgency, the resale motive behind the urgency is our structural inference and not their statement. No standby or interest list is evidenced to exist, so any build here creates its own input before it can produce anything.

opportunities.pain_source: Published hours 'Sunday - Saturday: 6:00am - 7:00/8:00pm'. Verified absence, no second line, no department routing, no answering service, no after-hours path other than voicemail, northcountrycharters.com/contact-1. Brian Ritchie published title 'Owner & Captain of The Irish'. Competitor verified, Central Charters takes instant online booking with a clickable August 2026 availability calendar and a 'Book with 10% deposit, pay rest to captain' checkout.

opportunities.notes: Satisfaction is deliberately mid, not low. FareHarbor already covers the self-serve booker, which is the parity point. Being on the water is a structural read of a published title, not a claim anyone made.

opportunities.job: As the person who handles everything no one else wants to deal with, I need the mechanical parts of that off my plate
opportunities.pain_source: Verbatim, 'Kathy is the co-owner and office manager, which loosely translates to: the person who handles everything no one else wants to deal with.' northcountrycharters.com/names-you-might-know
opportunities.notes: The job is real and first-party. It is also broad, and the specific tasks inside it are not published, so it cannot be scoped from this evidence alone. It scores as a container for other jobs rather than a build target of its own.

opportunities.job: When a charter guest needs a bed, I want them in my Guest Room and not someone else's
opportunities.pain_source: Home page lists exactly four things sold, Halibut Fishing, Combo Fishing, Salmon Fishing and a Guest Room, northcountrycharters.com
opportunities.notes: Thin. The only evidence is that the product exists. Nothing verified about attach rate, occupancy or whether this is a problem. Rides to the Later lane, not to a build.

opportunities.job: When a guest asks the same twenty pre-trip questions, I want them answered without anyone typing
opportunities.pain_source: The existence and detail of their FAQ, which carries policy, weather and cancellation rules, northcountrycharters.com/faq
opportunities.current_workaround: The FAQ page itself, plus the phone.
opportunities.notes: Deliberately scored low and this is the honest killer of the generic chatbot. The FAQ already serves it, and FareHarbor Agent is described as doing exactly this on a platform they already pay for. Selling them a guest-question bot would be selling them their own vendor's roadmap.

opportunities.job: I need to know which channel my bookings actually come from
opportunities.pain_source: Structural, three inbound paths exist in evidence, FareHarbor, the phone and one shared inbox, with nothing published that consolidates them
opportunities.notes: Weakest evidence in the set, included for completeness. Worth noting that the top-ranked build produces this as a by-product rather than needing its own project.

target_opportunity.job: No money-governed message sits unseen. Every cancellation, change or no-show risk that arrives on any channel gets to a human inside the window that decides the money, the 14-day line and the 24-hour line their own FAQ sets.
target_opportunity.why: It tops Ulwick at 15, and it is the only opportunity in the set whose evidence is the company's own written words about its own channel rather than an inference or a competitor's behaviour. Torres cross-check. Sizing, it touches every booking, not a subset. Market position, it is not the booking mechanic, where they are at parity with four verified FareHarbor competitors, and it is not generic guest Q&A, which is what FareHarbor's own page describes FareHarbor Agent doing, so it is the one high-value job that does not get erased if their existing vendor ships. Strategy fit, it is workflow automation, the unglamorous middle of the AI ladder, not a voice-agent bet. How much they care versus how satisfied, they cared enough to publish a policy apologising for the channel and asking customers to work around it, which is a company telling you where it hurts without ever claiming to be overwhelmed. Held to the drift warning, this is structural evidence about a message channel, and nothing here asserts or implies that this business is overwhelmed or misses calls.
target_opportunity.forces: Push, their own FAQ says voicemails and emails are not always seen right away and that every minute counts, and the money moves at 14 days and again at 24 hours, so lateness is expensive in both directions. Pull, a system that watches the Gmail and the voicemail they already have and makes their own phones ring for the messages that cost money, with nothing new to sign into. Anxiety, two sources and both are real. The MDPI finding is their anxiety in peer-reviewed form, a machine talking to an upset customer, and the second is paying us for something FareHarbor might include. Lower the first by designing the build so it never speaks to a guest about bad news, it alerts the owners and it acknowledges receipt in the company's own published wording. Lower the second by scoping deliberately around FareHarbor Agent's stated function and by writing into the deal what it replaces if it reaches them. Habit, the largest force against us by far, a phone and a person since 1979, two owners, one of them on the water. The only way push plus pull beats anxiety plus habit here is if the build requires zero change in behaviour. If it adds a dashboard someone has to remember to open, habit wins and the build fails. That is a design constraint, not a preference.

candidates.name: The 14-Day Clock
candidates.our_build: Workflow automation, an LLM in fixed classification steps, not an agent
candidates.what_it_does: Watches the shared Gmail inbox and voicemail transcripts they already have. Classifies each message against their own published policy, and for anything money-governed, a cancellation, a date change, a party-size change or a no-show risk, it does three things and stops. It stamps the message against the 14-day and 24-hour lines, it rings and texts Brian and Kathy with a one-line summary and the deadline, and it sends the guest an immediate acknowledgement in the company's own FAQ wording asking them to call and confirm by phone. It never negotiates, never quotes a price, never delivers bad news and never touches a refund. Everything non-urgent goes to one quiet daily digest. No new phone number, no new inbox, no new app, no behaviour change, and an off switch that takes a minute.

rice.reach: 100 index, every inbound contact on both channels is classified, and 100 percent of money-governed messages are routed
rice.impact: 2, massive on the primary metric, it is the only candidate aimed straight at median minutes to human confirmation, and it creates the baseline that every other build needs
rice.confidence: 0.85, the highest in the set, the driving evidence is a contiguous verbatim quote on the company's own FAQ plus two published money thresholds, with no inference in the chain
rice.effort: 2 person-weeks, read-only on an existing mailbox, no FareHarbor write access needed for v1

candidates.cost_of_delay: Moderate to high and two-sided. Landing in late August buys roughly three to four weeks of in-season proof before the mid-September close. Missing that means no in-season baseline exists until May 2027, a nine-month loss of the evidence that funds every later phase, which is a worse cost than the missed cancellations themselves.

provisional_pick.name: The 14-Day Clock
provisional_pick.why_over_others: It wins on RICE at 85, and more importantly it wins on the reasoning behind the numbers. Over the voice agent at 6.6, which is the loud, obvious answer and the one this evidence argues against hardest. Confidence killed it, not taste. It duplicates the function FareHarbor's own page describes FareHarbor Agent performing on a platform they already pay for, it puts a machine on the channel where weather and cancellation land at exactly the moment the one peer-reviewed tourism study in the package says to keep a human, its only supporting outcome data is vendor-published and out of industry, and it asks a two-person shop to change how its phone works with six weeks of season left. Over the off-season desk at 12.4, which has the better timing window and is the strongest Next item. It loses now on two counts, it overlaps FareHarbor Agent's stated territory more than any other candidate, and its competitive half proves what Emerald Air Service chose rather than what North Country needs, while the Clock's evidence is North Country's own sentence about its own channel. Over the weather fan-out at 12, which touches the highest-stakes moment in the business first, before anything is measured. That is the wrong order, and it becomes the obvious Next once the Clock is logging what actually arrives. Over the standby filler at 7.5, whose value window is the six weeks already running out and whose input list does not exist yet. Over do-nothing at 40, and this is the honest part. It scores that high only because it costs almost nothing, and we recommend they pursue it in parallel, which no pitch would say. It can't be the pick because we cannot deliver it, they may not be in the select group, and it has no published measurement anywhere. The Clock is deliberately designed so that answer does not make it redundant. If FareHarbor Agent reaches them, it answers guest questions and pushes booking links, and it is not described as watching their Gmail and their voicemail against their own 14-day and 24-hour money lines and making the owners' phones ring. Size discipline holds. One workflow, read-only on a mailbox they already have, alerts to phones they already carry, no new number, no new app, no new hire, and an off switch. That is buildable and adoptable by two people inside a season that closes mid-September.
